title: Raw DXF object name retained-budget fast slice
scope: Parser-side raw-carrier constructor census, generated no-group regression for name-only raw OBJECTS records, and a bounded writer-side materializer audit.

implementation.finding: All parser-side DRW_RawDxfObject record paths found in src/libdxfrw.cpp use copyRawDxfCarrierName() before body consumption. The empty unknown-object route has no captureRawGroup() call and therefore needs a direct name-lease regression.
implementation.test: testRawDxfObjectNameRetainedBudget() locates the minimum successful retained-byte budget for a generated AC1009 empty unknown OBJECTS record, asserts the published lease contains exactly the object-name bytes, and verifies one byte below the threshold fails with dxf-retained-byte-budget before callback publication.
implementation.follow_on_writer_audit: makeRawProxyObject() emits at most the three-object closure and validates each of its three possible binary source vectors against the 64 MiB per-payload ceiling. Hex chunk text is at most 2x payload bytes and allocation exceptions are caught by the enclosing closure materializer. This is a composable logical-size ceiling, not an allocator-capacity/RSS guarantee; no additional arbitrary aggregate cap was added.

non_claims: No parser behavior or support claim changed.
No allocator-capacity or RSS bound is claimed.
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain DEFERRED_EXTERNAL and non-promoting.

The shared worktree has extensive pre-existing changes. The sandbox denied creation of .git/index.lock, so no staging or commit occurred; keep any later commit isolated to this test, plan entry, and receipt.
